text: A proof by mathematical induction has two parts: the ___ case, in which one proves P(0), and the inductive step, in which one proves P(n) → P(n+1).
explanation: The base case establishes the property at the starting value (P(0)); omitting it is a classic error (as in the all-horses-are-the-same-color fallacy), since the inductive step alone proves nothing without a foundation to build on.
